briefs: Create a luminous architectural print: saturated colour fields, careful structural linework, real curves and unusually attentive window/cornice detail. Keep the image alive rather than diagrammatic.

Create a colour-led architectural portrait with the confidence and economy of an expressive print. Use larger warm/cool colour relationships, atmospheric light, layered ink or dry-brush decisions, and selective rather than blanket detail. Let quiet planes remain quiet. Preserve the distinctive silhouette, major curves, openings and viewpoint; use a few crisp structural accents so expressiveness does not become wonky geometry. Do not increase hatch density or brick counts just to look detailed. Aim for a painting worth keeping, not an inventory diagram. Keep colour immersive, and make your own compositional and mark-making choices.

experiment.decisionBasis: Latest answer per pair: existing brief preferred 4, tie 4, previous extra-guided brief preferred 0. Ten append-only events represent eight comparisons, not ten independent labels. No evidence that more prescriptive detail guidance helped.
experiment.hypothesis: Keep the working baseline and explore colour-led economy, not further detail prescription. This is a new art-direction comparison, not a trained policy or an isolated causal estimate.
experiment.selection: Eight new source posts selected before generation for contrast; all previously painted posts excluded. Not a random sample; foundation-model pretraining overlap is unknown.
experiment.protocol: One fresh program per arm/source, one own-render revision opportunity; same model, medium, resource limits. Counterbalanced A/B. Retain all failures and successful fallback versions. Max32 painting-model requests; no automatic training.
